title: Luxury Brands Slow Down Their Price Increases

source.author: Julia Garel
source.title: Study: Can luxury brands still raise their prices?
source.checked_against: Single source. Web search on 2026-11-13 found no second outlet carrying the November 2026 Retviews by Lectra study; earlier Retviews reports (2023-2025) describe the same pattern (China the most expensive market, gap with Europe narrowing) but give no figures for 2026, so no figure was cross-checked or taken from them. Author and publication date come from the page metadata (the page shows no byline). The article notes it was partly written with an AI tool and then fact-checked and edited by a FashionUnited journalist.

paragraphs: For three years, luxury brands had a simple habit. When they wanted to grow, they raised their prices. Few of them could resist it. A new study says this habit is now changing. The study comes from Retviews, a tool from the company Lectra that follows prices in fashion. FashionUnited wrote about it on November 12, 2026.

First, look at why prices matter so much. According to a report by The Business of Fashion and McKinsey, about 80% of the growth in the luxury market between 2023 and 2025 came from higher prices. It did not come from selling more items. In other words, brands earned more mostly because each buyer paid more.
One famous bag demonstrates this. Prada's Cleo bag cost 1,847 dollars in 2021. In 2026, it costs 3,001 dollars. That is a remarkable increase of 62%. Can a brand justify such a climb?

Now the increases come less often. Several brands used to raise the price of their signature bags twice a year. Since 2025, they have done it only once a year. Big increases are also less common in luxury than in the rest of fashion. Only 18% of luxury leaders plan to raise prices by more than 5% in 2026. For fashion as a whole, the number is 26%.

The study also compared prices in distinct markets. It looked at five brands and used Europe as the base. The same bag does not have an identical price around the world. China is the most expensive market for all five brands. A Miu Miu product costs about 50% more in China than in Europe, on average. For Burberry, the gap is 45%. For Loewe and Prada, it is 40%. For Chloé, it is 34%.

Nevertheless, this gap is getting smaller. In 2025, a Prada product in China cost 54% more than in Europe, on average. In 2026, it costs 40% more. Prices are still not identical, but they are closer. Japan is a distinct case. It is the only market where several brands are cheaper than in Europe. Miu Miu costs 7% less there. Burberry and Loewe cost 5% less.

Why are brands changing? The report links the change to what buyers now expect. In the past, a luxury bag was mostly a symbol of social status. Today, that is not enough. People want to feel close to a brand. They also want it to show who they are. A status symbol alone does not justify a very high price for them.

The study highlights a clear point. Luxury brands can still raise prices, but they do it more slowly and with more care. They are also adding more accessible products. Accessible here means easier to buy, at a lower price. Some brands may not resist raising prices again. But a signature bag is already very expensive. If prices keep rising every year, some buyers may stop following the climb.
